title: South gate pocket route guide
central_assumption: A guide offered through the ordinary south gate flow will be taken without a research prompt, kept, and used at later route choices by visitors who need a step-free refill route. Uptake, retention, gate throughput, and paper handling capacity are unverified.
proposal: Develop a small, high-contrast paper guide offered to visitors during the ordinary south gate entry flow. Its front shows a water symbol, a bold 'step-free paved route' label, and a simple traced line from 'You are here: south gate' to the staffed West Canopy refill point. Mark the lawn shortcut as not step-free, and show the paved route's estimated four extra minutes without suggesting that this is a measured universal travel time. Put brief directions and a return-to-gate cue on the reverse. The paved route to West Canopy is documented as step-free, but the packet supplies no turns or decision-point geometry; trace and check the line on site before printing. West Canopy is only a candidate for the required shaded destination: its name does not prove shade. Do not label the guide 'shaded refill' or distribute it for that purpose until shade is checked. Leave opening times off until decided; any gate-staff service-information procedure must be confirmed as feasible. The portable guide does not rely on installed route signs, a phone, or connectivity. If ordinary gate delivery fails the uptake and later-use trial, stop the gate-only concept and compare a different physical wayfinding approach rather than treating guided test success as proof of deployment feasibility.
dependencies: Verify that West Canopy actually offers shade at the refill location and during intended use; the source does not establish shade from its name.
Trace the paved south gate to West Canopy route, identify every decision point, and check the printed diagram with wheelchair users before issuing it. The packet gives no route geometry.

Confirm gate permission, staff duties, print quantity, replenishment, weather protection, and collection or disposal capacity. Paper handling capacity is unverified; a once-morning paper-sign update allowance does not establish handout capacity.
Obtain a complete priced total within £8,000, including design, printing, gate distribution, replenishment, collection, and removal. Affordability is unverified.
Decide and communicate refill-point operating hours before any time-specific claim. Hours are unverified, including after the evening performance.
Obtain management approval before deployment; no design has been approved.
risks: A visitor can complete a prompted guide trial yet miss the guide during normal entry or discard it before a later decision.
A guide-only design gives no route cue at decision points to someone without a copy.
A diagram with unverified turns could send visitors onto the non-step-free lawn shortcut.
Printing an unverified shade or opening-hours claim would misrepresent the destination.
Gate distribution, replenishment, discarded-paper collection, or full costs may exceed available capacity or the cap.
A printed guide may become stale if route access or refill service changes during the day.
rough_effort: One on-site route trace and shade check, one guide layout and print proof, a bounded ordinary-gate uptake and later-use observation plus a wheelchair-route trial, and a full cost and operations check before any three-week pilot. No time or cost estimate is established by the packet.
falsifying_test: After tracing the route and creating a proof, observe ordinary south gate entry during two contrasting gate periods agreed with operations. Use the normal proposed handout procedure, with no researcher prompt to take or retain a guide. Count arrivals, offers, acceptances, refusals, stock gaps, and distribution delays; ask an exit sample whether they sought refill guidance. At every traced route decision point, unobtrusively record whether visitors who accepted a guide still have it, consult it, and choose the paved route; use a short exit interview to distinguish guide use from lucky route choice. Separately trial the traced line with wheelchair users without installed route signs. Check the actual gate task load, replenishment, wet-guide protection, and discarded-paper collection during both periods. Proposed no-go criteria for this test, not source facts: a visitor seeking the step-free refill route misses a guide in normal entry, lacks usable guidance at a later choice and takes or cannot rule out the lawn shortcut, or cannot follow the paved line with the guide; distribution interrupts essential gate work; stock or collection cannot be maintained; or paper is left without an assigned handling process. Any such outcome defeats the gate-only mechanism and calls for revision or a different physical approach. The small test cannot prove site-wide reliability, so do not deploy unless the separate shade, route accuracy, operating-hours, full-cost including distribution and removal within £8,000, paper-capacity, and management-approval gates also clear.
